back: Haloalkanes and haloarenes may be classified as mono, di, or polyhalogen compounds depending on whether they contain one, two or more halogen atoms in their structures.
front: What is the classification of haloalkanes and haloarenes?

back: Alkyl halides contain halogen atoms attached to sp3-hybridised carbon atoms of an alkyl group, while aryl halides contain halogen atoms attached to sp2-hybridised carbon atoms of an aromatic ring.
front: What is the difference between alkyl halides and aryl halides?

back: Common names of alkyl halides are derived by naming the alkyl group followed by the halide.
front: How are common names of alkyl halides derived?

back: Haloarenes are named as halosubstituted hydrocarbons in the IUPAC system of nomenclature.
front: What is the IUPAC system of nomenclature for haloarenes?

back: Geminal halides have halogen atoms present on the same carbon atom, while vicinal halides have halogen atoms present on adjacent carbon atoms.
front: What is the difference between geminal and vicinal halides?
